calls.title: TLC: The Haystack Paradox: What happens after AI creates a million ads with Juliana J
calls.summary: The meeting explored the significance of creative intelligence in marketing, highlighting that creative assets are crucial for campaign performance yet often under-measured. Reports indicate that creative drives 50% of performance, yet most companies reset learnings after each campaign. Traditional funnel models are deemed outdated and need a shift toward algorithmic and exploratory approaches. While multi-armed bandits are limited in understanding ad success, effective labeling and taxonomy are vital for measuring asset performance. AI-powered labeling, combined with human oversight, ensures quality, while historical data enables learning and compounding knowledge across campaigns. The emphasis shifted from mere optimization to embracing creative exploration for sustainable growth amidst changing media landscapes.
calls.keywords: creative intelligence, generative AI, content labeling, response surface methodology, multi-armed bandit, campaign optimization

calls.title: TLC: 5 Stories to Rewire Your Statistical Intuition with Ishan Goel
calls.summary: The meeting emphasized the importance of statistical fundamentals in experimentation, primarily addressing issues like sampling bias, the interpretation of null results, and the impact of false positive and negative errors. Ishan Goel highlighted that experiments provide a limited data view, making randomization essential to reduce internal bias, while also stressing that absence of evidence doesn't indicate no effect exists. The role of error costs in shaping experiment designs was explored, along with the significance of variance and outlier analysis in understanding average metrics. The discussions also contrasted Bayesian and frequentist approaches, highlighting the challenges faced in applying Bayesian methods while addressing false discovery risks related to declared winners. Overall, the session aimed to deepen participants' statistical intuition for more effective experimentation.
calls.keywords: statistical intuition, A/B testing, false discovery rate, experiment design, Bayesian statistics, data variance
